subject.title: Cron job reports failure when using env var for Discord channel, even on success

question: Should cron `delivery.to` support `env:` or SecretRef-backed recipient indirection for Discord targets, or should that syntax be rejected with a clear diagnostic?
rationale: Current docs and source support explicit target strings, while env-backed recipient resolution would expand config/secret semantics and cannot be chosen safely by cleanup automation.

options.title: Reject env targets for now
options.body: Add or keep validation that tells users to use explicit `channel:<id>` or `user:<id>` targets until a broader SecretRef target contract is designed.

options.title: Support env/SecretRef targets
options.body: Define and implement secure cron delivery target indirection with redaction, validation, docs, focused tests, and live Discord proof.

options.title: Coordinate with delivery-default work
options.body: Let adjacent cron delivery-error/default changes proceed separately while keeping this issue open for the env-target contract decision.

recommendation.title: Reject env targets for now
recommendation.body: Add or keep validation that tells users to use explicit `channel:<id>` or `user:<id>` targets until a broader SecretRef target contract is designed.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent target API work touched the Discord, plugin contract, outbound resolver, and cron delivery boundaries involved in this decision.
